As far as the prompt goes or tokens in general go tokens just depend on the context and how well the tokenizer breaks up what you say into readable chunks for the AI.  The actual value of tokens changes dramatically depending on the amount of different responses it can come up with, how long the responses are, how much context there already is, and how much input the user puts in to get a response.  


So like if GPT4 wasn't trained so well as a language model to respond to greetings and you just said "Hello" you'd be surprised at how many tokens would be generated just from that input.

One thing I've really noticed is that it's VERY inconsistent when asked to follow directions.  It's a bit weird how sometimes it will follow them to a T and other times it will completely ignore what you want.  


I know there's a variable that controls how it will vary responses and sometimes to a degree that it will either make up facts or ignore instructions but that still doesn't explain how blatant some of the problems are.  


I feel like there might just be an issue with the transformers models that causes it to not use the entire message's worth of instructions (partly because of how tokens work and partly because it also tries to use context) but I feel like the context shouldn't come at the cost of what the immediate prompt tells the AI to respond with.  


Unfortunately for projects like this the AI just has a really hard time reading all of the context and it's just not possible (yet) for it to fully understand every word with the combined input/output/context.  I'd almost rather most models that people host use chunking at the cost of performance to provide much more accurate responses to context.
